# Move the generated [Phrase] link into the source map; the grammar and the bench scorer follow
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #166, sha256:74ae83a9b13fc89ec1afe706ca7810e329f7eae2afe268a8eb0755763c351dc6). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (sequenced with card 162 by the Decider; touches the emitter, the bench scorer, the reference output and the frozen grammar through a re-freeze)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Product design principle (Decider D111): generated code must not know about the layers that depend on or produce it. The generated `[Phrase("...")]` attribute and its runtime class carry knowledge of the Phrase source in the C#: the same inverted dependency. Raised while reviewing card 161 (2026-10-28), whose scope was kept to the source map and the output kept unchanged.
- **Depends on:** 161, 162
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want the link from a generated symbol back to its phrase to live in the source map and not in the generated C#, so that the runtime stays ignorant of the authoring layer and I still trace a failure to its phrase with phrase trace.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the C# adapter, When it emits endpoints and phrases, Then no `[Phrase(...)]` attribute and no generated `PhraseAttribute` class appear in the output, the template text each attribute carried is a field of the matching source map record (so phrase trace prints it), the benchmark scorer and every other reader that looked for the attribute read the map instead, and the reference sources under reference/csharp are regenerated
  2. Given docs/GRAMMAR.md line 256 and the cheat sheet, When card 162 re-freezes them, Then they stop describing the attribute and describe the source map and phrase trace instead (one re-freeze Decider and one rerun of the LLM check cover both cards; the Usable v1 bar 6 evidence is regenerated)
  3. Given the per-step comments and the header comment naming the module, When they are reviewed, Then each is judged by one rule: a comment that is plain readability text with no Phrase coupling (it would read the same to someone who never saw a .phrase file) may stay; a comment that copies the Phrase source text of a step or names the .phrase file is moved to the map. The Decider records the verdict for each kind. The orders output hash is re-recorded once, with the exact change named, and the 422 bodies and the 11 specs stay unchanged
